transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, November 3. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Heavy rainfall, uprooted trees, power outages: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast. The cyclonic storm MURASU took a north-northwest path, striking south Andhra Pradesh early Tuesday. This powerful storm brought substantial rainfall, with some regions receiving over 16 cm, leading to significant disruptions. Wind speeds reached alarming levels, initially between 100-110 kmph and gusts up to 120 kmph. As the storm weakens into a deep depression by midnight, residents in low-lying areas are urged to brace for potential flooding. Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees, borrows $25 billion to fuel AI push. Microsoft has priced a $25 billion bond sale, its first US investment-grade offering since 2017, just days after offering voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees. Orders hit $115 billion across ten tranches, while CFO Amy Hood flagged Azure demand outpacing supply. The money will fund AI data centre spending as capex nears $175 billion. Disney weighs thousands of job cuts, asks managers to target 20 percent cost savings. Walt Disney is embarking on a significant cost-saving initiative that may lead to thousands of job cuts. Managers have received directives to pinpoint strategies that can achieve a 20 percent decrease in yearly expenses. This restructuring is a response to ongoing challenges in sectors such as streaming and theme parks. Nagaland man, 90, turns wife's grave into flower garden tourist spot. At the age of 90, Mosenyii Yakhro dedicates his life to nurturing a garden around his late wife's grave in Nagaland, a beautiful spot now known as Mosen Viewpoint. Attracting both locals and tourists, this vibrant space sees families, especially on his birthday each year, paying homage and creating cherished memories. His devotion encapsulates an enduring love and highlights the significance of preserving precious moments. Florida jet 'broke apart' midair before crashing into roadway; victims identified. A Learjet 60 carrying nine people may have started breaking apart mid-air before plunging into a Florida roadway and erupting into a fireball, federal investigators said on Monday. ' rupees 14,000cr loss last month': Delhi traders seek protest-free Delhi till Nov 11. Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) on Tuesday wrote to Delhi Police Commissioner, seeking a ban on rallies, sit-ins, protests and marches across the national capital until November 11. Top stocks to buy today: Stock market recommendations for Nov 3 - check list. Stock market recommendations: Adani Green, DLF, Hindalco, and BPCL are the top stocks to buy today as per recommendations by Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research, Mirae Asset ShareKhan for November 3, 2026. US launches 'secret' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as peace talks teeter along. The United States launched "secret" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing US officials, amid renewed tensions over the possibility of fresh military action against Tehran. Prince William sorry as Bradninch Estate sale sparks tenant backlash. Prince William has apologised following backlash over the Duchy of Cornwall's plan to sell the 3,000-acre Bradninch Estate in Devon. Tenants are demanding fair property valuations, while King Charles is reportedly disappointed by the decision. The proposed sale has also raised questions over the Duchy's claimed exemption from capital gains tax. AIFF bid to break rupees 20 crore FD to pay Brazil, Uruguay for friendlies stalled. The All India Football Federation's proposal to break its fixed deposit of rupees 20 crore to pay Brazil and Uruguay for last month's international friendlies was stalled by general body members, who said such a move could be allowed only in an emergency. Canadian woman sets world record with 44.1-decibel nose whistle. LuLu Lotus, who discovered her unique talent as a child, achieved the Guinness World Record for the loudest nose whistle. She successfully recorded a whistle measuring 44.1 decibels, impressing many with her skills. This remarkable talent led her to collaborate with Aercoustics Engineering Ltd. for precise measurements.

IPO fundraising rises 30 percent to record rupees 84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report. India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at rupees 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat. As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago. According to the report, the funds raised increased from rupees 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to rupees 84,400 crore in H1 FY27. The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said.
